english.title: Possess a dangerous article in an aircraft - Aviation Security Act 1982

english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1)(a), (b), (2) and (4) of the Aviation Security Act 1982.

english.notes:
(i) Section 4(1) of the Aviation Security Act 1982 provides that the onus of proof that a defendant had lawful authority or reasonable excuse to possessed any article lies with him /her.
(ii) In respect of an aircraft registered in the United Kingdom the offence is complete whether the aircraft is in the United Kingdom or not.
(iii) In respect of an aircraft NOT registered in the United Kingdom the offence is complete at a time when it is in, or in flight over, the United Kingdom.
(iv) Section 4(3) provides that "possession" will be include circumstances where in offending article is being carried within the defendant's baggage or any other property to be carried on the flight.
(v) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
